Having a treaty that guarantees neutrality underwritten by the Great Powers is not ironclad. In 1839, the Treaty of London guaranteed the newly created state of Belgium independence and neutrality. It was signed by the Great Powers: the UK, France, Austria-Hungary, Russia, Prussia. Up until 1914, Belgium was often called 'Switzerland by the North Sea'.

However in 1914, two of the signatories, Germany and Austria-Hungary broke the treaty and moreover invaded Belgium without cause, making a mockery of the Treaty they had co-signed.

So in the case of Switzerland, there must have been other factors that made the signatories of treaties honor those treaties.
